title: For Valorant, prioritize smaller flicks, switching, and click timing over flashy wide flicks
summary: Tactical shooters reward small, clean flicks and stable finishes far more often than dramatic wide-angle flicks, so a Valorant routine should lean toward switching and click-timing work that teaches tension control and precise finishing.
why: Viscose points out that smaller flick management matters heavily in Counter-Strike and Valorant, especially for tension control and clean target finish quality.
Click-timing and stability-oriented work often transfers better to tactical shooters because the player needs precise placement and controlled follow-through more than raw spectacle.
actions: Make small-flick switching and click-timing precision the center of a Valorant playlist.
Favor drills that punish messy landings, extra micro-corrections, and unstable finish quality rather than only rewarding raw speed.
Use tracking as supplementary mouse-control support, not the main source of tactical-shooter improvement.
avoid: Do not judge transfer quality only by how exciting or difficult a scenario looks.
Avoid over-indexing on wide flashy flick tasks if most of your misses are on small or medium adjustments.
